summary: Phases 1-2 completed cleanly: full 550-test oracle suite run under -n 6 finished in 44:33 (2673.06s), yielding 7 failed, 534 passed, 9 xfailed. Phase 3 triage is DONE and reached rubric category (c) -- a genuine, refactor-introduced regression -- so the task cannot close. Systematic isolated re-runs (5 pytest invocations total) found: (1) the 5 failures NOT on the plan's watch list are benign -n 6 parallel-execution artifacts (all pass together in one serial re-run, 2:59); (2) BOTH plan-designated 'known contention flake' watch-list tests fail deterministically in isolation, falsifying that classification entirely; (3) a baseline-commit check at pre-refactor commit 6cfb7f48 (read-only git worktree) shows test_all_sat_task_relation_ternary passes there but fails on the current branch -- a refactor-introduced regression -- while test_complexity_5_scan_self_consistent fails at both commits (pre-existing, refactor not implicated, though the disagreement count differs 1-vs-3 across a single sample each and is left as an open question). No baseline was promoted, no Phase 2 marker was flipped in the refactor plan, and Phases 4-6 did not run, per the rubric's category (c) action. -n 6 is now demonstrated unsound for this suite's baseline generation (5 false failures); recommendation is a serial baseline run or xdist_group serialization markers on the affected test classes.

blockers.description: test_all_sat_task_relation_ternary (test_oracle_interface.py::TestTernarySerializationAll) is a refactor-introduced regression: PASSES at pre-refactor commit 6cfb7f48, FAILS on the current branch with AssertionError 'Expected SAT for next_A' (assert None is not None) -- find_countermodel returns no model for a next_A (temporal diamond over atom A) formula expected SAT. This is rubric category (c): a hard stop. No baseline can be promoted and the refactor plan's Phase 2 markers cannot be flipped until this is fixed.
